name: AbilityListRow
summary: One 8-byte row of the job screen's ability page: word 0 job id, word 1 ability id with flag bits; the list ends with {0, 0xFFFF}.

members.name: job_id
members.text: Job the row belongs to; sub_14028A474 stores the tab's job id, sub_14028A8B0 stores the unit's job for the first row of a tab.

members.name: ability_word
members.text: Ability id with 0x1000 (known), 0x4000 (not learnable / already known) or 0x6000 (hidden), set by sub_14028A474 (0x14028A61B-0x14028A678) and sub_14028A8B0 (0x14028A9F7-0x14028AA06).

members.name: padding
members.text: Zero; the row is moved as a qword by the sorter (0x14028AB74-0x14028AB7F).

behavior.text: the row is an address-taken record: sub_14028A8B0 swaps whole qwords, so the flag bits travel with the id, while the sort key masks the id.
sub_14028A8B0 de-duplicates on the raw ability word, so the same id with different flags is kept twice.

notes: V: see the sheets sub_14028A474, sub_14028A8B0 and JobScreen_BuildJobTabRows.
open_questions: ? who reads 0x1000 / 0x4000 / 0x6000 on these rows; the consumers are outside the exported set.

name: ActionEntryWord
summary: The 16-bit word of a four-byte action entry (the AI and preview form): the action id in bits 0..9 and the acting unit slot in bits 10..15. The current-action builder splits it with a 10-bit mask and a shift of ten.

members.name: action_id
members.text: Item id, ability id or throw item id depending on the command; the builder masks it with 0x3FF.

members.name: acting_unit
members.text: Acting unit slot, taken by a right shift of ten. A width census labels these six bits an action kind; the decoded reader uses them as the unit slot, and the record follows the reader.

behavior.text: the entry is four bytes: this word, a command byte and a flags byte. The builder stores the command byte at block +0, the word at +2 and the flags at +0x10.
only ten id bits are ever read, so a raw id above 1023 cannot reach the builder through this word.
for the Item command the word holds an ability id (item + 0x80) at use; the builder subtracts 0x80 to recover the item id, stores the item at block +6 and keeps the ability in the word.
for Throw the low ten bits are an item id first and become the resolved throw ability, so the word and the item field at +6 disagree about what the low bits mean until the ability is resolved.
a six-bit field cannot be both a unit slot and an action kind; the unit-slot reading is the decoded one, so the kind label in the width census is a naming error rather than a second meaning.

notes: V: the sheet Action_BuildCurrentAction (layout and the item/throw branches).
open_questions: ? whether any other producer packs a different field into bits 10..15 (the width census's kind).

name: ActionResult
summary: The result of one action on one target, filled by the formula handler and read by the result applier, the preview and the messages. One lives at +0x1BE of each battle unit record (g_BattleActionBlock points at the target's); a second, the caster's own result, is a separate static block (g_BattleCasterResult). Battle_ResultReset sets it up before the handler runs: hit flag 1, hit percent 100, nearly everything else 0.

members.name: hit
members.text: 1 = the effect lands, 0 = nothing happens. Battle_ResultReset stores 1; every miss path stores 0 (Formula_EvadeByteRoll, Formula_ChanceRoll, Formula_ZeroResult, Formula_StealGate).

members.name: critical
members.text: Set to 1 by Formula_CritRoll.

members.name: miss_reason
members.text: The reason when hit is 0: 1..4 an evade by evade byte k (Formula_EvadeRoll), 5 nullified (Formula_ZeroResult), 6 failed the chance roll (Formula_ChanceRoll, Formula_BardDancerGate), 7 no effect, 8 the caster-side katana result (Formula_DrawOutGate on the caster's block), 9, 11 and 13 reaction results. The meaning of each reason for the messages is I.

members.name: item_id
members.text: The picked equipment id of a steal or break (Action_PickTargetEquipment); on the caster's block the caster's word +0x1A8 (Formula_DrawOutGate).

members.name: hp_damage
members.text: HP damage (Formula_DamageAB; about 70 sites). Held at 0x7FFF by Formula_DamageAB and clamped to 999 by sub_14030A11C.

members.name: hp_heal
members.text: HP heal (Formula_HealSwap, Formula_DrainHP, Formula_FinalizeAbsorb).

members.name: mp_damage
members.text: MP damage (Formula_DrainMP and the MP formulas).

members.name: mp_heal
members.text: MP heal (Formula_DrainMP on the caster's block, the MP restore formulas).

members.name: gil
members.text: Gil change: the caster's block +gil, the target's block -gil (Formula_StealGilApply).

members.name: reaction_id
members.text: The reaction ability id to run after the result (440, 448..452 in the stock formulas 42 and 99 and in sub_14030AFEC).

members.name: flags
members.text: Flag word: 0x0002 recruit, 0x0004 equipment broken, 0x0008 draw-out kept, 0x0010 equipment stolen, 0x0040 status result, 0x0080, 0x0100 level drain, 0x0200 inflict roll passed (Formula_StatusChance19), 0x0400 absorbed (Formula_ElementAffinity), 0x0800 weak (doubled), 0x1000 draw-out katana broken, 0x2000 action failed banner, 0x4000 knockback present (Formula_KnockbackCalc). Stored by Formula_ElementAffinity, Formula_FinalizeAbsorb, Formula_StatusChance19, Formula_KnockbackCalc, Formula_56_StatusOnlyApplication and formulas 20, 37, 38, 46, 87, 88, 89.

members.name: speed_delta
members.text: A stat change: bit 7 = increase, the low 7 bits the amount. Written by formulas 57, 28 (ability 88), 29 (ability 95) and Formula_SapStatPick (143, 197). Which of +0x14 / +0x16 / +0x17 the game applies as which stat is I (the stock abilities that write each are known).

members.name: ct_delta
members.text: CT change: 0xFF = +127, 127 = -127 (formulas 18, 21, 93, 28 ability 92, 29 ability 99, 42 ability 117).

members.name: pa_delta
members.text: PA change (formulas 54, 85, 59; 28 ability 89; 29 ability 96; Formula_SapStatPick 144 / 198): Battle_ApplyActionResult applies it to the PA base +0x38 through Unit_ChangeBattleStat (cap 99, min 1).

members.name: ma_delta
members.text: MA change (formulas 86, 59; 28 ability 90; 29 ability 97; Formula_SapStatPick 145 / 199): applied to the MA base +0x39 through Unit_ChangeBattleStat (cap 99, min 1).

members.name: brave_delta
members.text: Brave change (formulas 58, 59, 97, 98 and 42 abilities 118 / 119).

members.name: faith_delta
members.text: Faith change (formula 42 abilities 120 / 121).

members.name: action_class
members.text: Stored by Battle_ResolveAction from dword_140787F84[2 * ability id] & 3, with 0x80 added when bit 0x1000000 of that dword is set, before the handler runs. Its meaning is ?.

members.name: equipment_slot_mask
members.text: The picked equipment slot of a steal or break: 0x80 head, 0x40 body, 0x20 accessory, 0x10 right weapon, 0x08 right shield, 0x04 left weapon, 0x02 left shield (Action_PickTargetEquipment; Formula_StealGate clears it).

members.name: status_add
members.text: The statuses to add: status s is bit 0x80 >> (s & 7) of byte s >> 3 (Formula_56_StatusOnlyApplication; sub_1403067D0 adds a bit in byte +0x1E).

members.name: status_remove
members.text: The statuses to remove (the name Status_FilterPendingSets gives the set at +34..38; bit 0x10 of the inflict flag copies the record into it). Formula_ElementAffinity sets bit 0x80 of byte +0x24 (I: status 16, Oil, so a doubled hit takes Oil away).

members.name: kind_bits
members.text: Result-kind bits: 0x80 HP damage, 0x40 HP heal, 0x20 MP damage, 0x10 MP heal, 0x08 status change pending, 0x01 another change (stat, gil, CT, EXP). Every routing block sets the matching bit with the amount.

members.name: reaction_copy
members.text: A copy of the reaction ability id (formula 99 writes 450 here and at +0x10); read by the message and reaction code.

members.name: exp_delta
members.text: EXP change: the amount ORed with 0x80 on the target's block (Formula_40_StealEXP).

members.name: hit_percent
members.text: The hit percent the preview shows and sub_14030A11C tests for 0 (it then clears the hit flag). Battle_ResultReset stores 100; Formula_EvadeRoll, Formula_BardDancerGate, Formula_ChanceRoll and Formula_56_StatusOnlyApplication scale it.

behavior.text: Battle_ResultReset (0x14030A410) clears the word at +1, the qword at +4 (+4..+0x0B), the dword at +0x0C, the qword at +0x12 (+0x12..+0x19), the word at +0x1A (+0x1A, +0x1B), the byte at +0x1C and the kind byte +0x27, stores 0x00640000 over the dword at +0x2A (hit percent 100) and 1 at +0, then calls sub_14030A43C, which clears the two status sets (+0x1D..+0x26) and a five-byte array at 0x14186B028. Not cleared: +0x03, the reaction id +0x10 and the copy +0x28 (so everything else is 0 after the reset except these three bytes).

Battle_ResolveAction resets both the target's block (g_BattleActionBlock) and the caster's static block (g_BattleCasterResult) before it runs the handler, so a handler may write the caster's own result without clearing it first.
the block is 0x30 bytes: the next field of the battle unit record after it is at +0x1EE (read as flag bits by sub_14030A11C).

after the handler (and sub_1403067D0 for ids below 7) sub_14030A11C(1) clamps the four amounts to 999, scales HP and MP damage by the difficulty row, runs the post hook of 12 formulas and clears the hit flag when the hit percent is 0; Battle_ResolveAction then ORs 1 into the kind byte (+0x27) when the flag word (+0x12) is non-zero (0x140309F84..0x140309F8B).
Unit_ChangeBattleStat applies +0x14 to Speed (+0x3A, cap 50), +0x15 to CT (+0x41), +0x16 to PA (+0x38), +0x17 to MA (+0x39), +0x18 to Brave (+0x2B), +0x19 to Faith (+0x2D).

notes: Read 2026-11-12. Offsets are relative to the start of the block, which is unit +0x1BE. The status sets and the array at 0x14186B028 are cleared by the reset through sub_14030A43C; the reaction id (+0x10) is not cleared by it.
open_questions: ? the meaning of +0x1A (action_class) and of the bytes +0x03, +0x1C, +0x28, +0x29 and +0x2B; what the five-byte array at 0x14186B028 holds (I: a staging copy of the pending status set).

name: AiCommandEntry
summary: One candidate action of the AI's command table: the ability word (id | unit slot << 10), the command (skillset) byte it comes from and a flag byte. A row of 34 entries per AI unit lives in g_AiCommandTable; the byte +2 = 0xFF of the entry after the last one ends the row.

members.name: word
members.text: The ability id in the low bits, the unit's slot << 10 above it (sub_140316D24 writes id | slot << 10, or slot << 10 alone for an entry with no ability, such as the Arithmeticks and Jump entries).

members.name: command
members.text: The command (skillset) byte the entry came from: 1 for the plain action of sub_140316B04's first entry, the unit's set for sub_140316D24's entries; 0xFF ends the row.

members.name: flags
members.text: Entry flags: the last entry holds 0x84 here (the word 0x84A9 stored at +2); sub_140316D24 sets bit 0x08 for the fourth list ability of a monster set (0xB0..0xDF) and clears it for the others. The other bits were not read.

behavior.text: the table is word_141872598 (g_AiCommandTable): 16 rows x 34 entries x 4 bytes, the row chosen by byte_141873038[unit slot]; an 8-byte header per row sits at byte_141872E20 (the item id word at header +4 is read by sub_140316D24 for the command kind 10 test).

sub_140316B04 writes entry 0 (command 1, word = slot << 10), then calls sub_140316D24 for the primary and (outside the monster range 0xB0..0xDF) the secondary set, then writes the last entry (word = (slot << 10) + 367, bytes +2 / +3 = 0xA9 / 0x84) and the 0xFF terminator when fewer than 34 entries are used.
readers of the command byte: 0x140320569, sub_14031FD40 (0x14031FED7), sub_14038D65C (0x14038D835); sub_140275EF4 (0x140276076) copies byte +2 to a unit's +0x13.

notes: Source: IDA reads of 2026-11-12. The row-header bytes other than the item word were not read.
open_questions: ? what a row header's bytes mean beyond the item word at +4; the readers of the table (sub_14038BC00, sub_14038C8F8, sub_14038D65C) were not read for this record.

name: AtlasShelf
summary: The state of one layer atlas allocator (a shelf / row packer): the cursor in the current row, the start of the row, the height of the row and the page. The UI manager holds two, the primary at +8616 and the secondary (masked layers only) at +8632; UIRender_PrepareLayers resets both every frame, GUILayer_PackAtlasRect and AtlasShelf_Alloc advance them.

members.name: cursor_x
members.text: Next free x in the current row (0 at the start of a page and of a row). Advances by the padded width plus the alignment pad.

members.name: row_y
members.text: Top of the current row (0 at the start of a page). Grows by the row height when a row is closed.

members.name: row_height
members.text: Height of the tallest rectangle in the current row, margins and alignment pad included; 0 for a new row.

members.name: page
members.text: Page index (0 at the start of the frame); +1 each time a rectangle does not fit below the current row.

behavior.text: the starting state of both shelves is {0, 0, 0, 0}: UIRender_PrepareLayers and the UI renderer constructor copy the zero pair g_ZeroPair into cursor_x / row_y and clear the row height (the page index is cleared by the same stores).

the primary shelf read {674, 239, 251, 4}: page 4, row top 239, row height 251, cursor 674. That is the state after the last layer of the list (slot 62, integer rectangle 610 x 187, margin 32, the first layer of its row: cursor 0 + 610 + 64 = 674, row top 239, row height 187 + 64 = 251); a model of the placement reproduces the whole state. The secondary shelf read {0, 0, 0, 0} (no masked layer in the frame).

notes: Detail and evidence: the function sheets linked from this page.

name: BattleMsgDescriptor
summary: The 4-dword descriptor the banner takes: class, subtype, kind and a message word. The banner resolves it to a template through a class/subtype switch; class 0 subtype 2 turns the kind and the word's low 11 bits into a table-172 message id, class 1 subtype 27 is a UI text id and class 1 subtype 171 a table-172 key.

members.name: class
members.text: 0 or 1 in the studied code. The text resolver switches on this together with the subtype (V, decompile).

members.name: subtype
members.text: 2 (event-script message id), 27 (UI text id) or 171 (direct table-172 key) in the studied code (V, decompile).

members.name: kind
members.text: Message kind. For class 0 subtype 2 it is the multiplier of the 1000-wide message-id base; only the kinds in registry BattleMsgKindBase give an id (V, decompile).

members.name: word
members.text: Message word, read as a u16 and masked with 0x7FF: the row index below the kind's base, or a table-172 key for class 1 subtype 171 (V, decompile and live trace).

behavior.basis: (live trace 2026-10-31, tracepoint on the banner function, one call during an ability cast)

behavior.text: 0x5062 packs group 10 in bits 11 and up and index 98 in the low 11 bits, an event-script message.
whether the traced call was produced by the ability cast. The code that builds the banner descriptor for an ability cast is not identified.

notes: V: a producer of descriptors of this shape is the scene task SceneMsgTask_Run. It reads the current scene task record's u16 at +28 as the word, takes group = word >> 11 to select one of the group objects at qword_140D40990, uses index = word & 0x7FF, asks the group object (sub_1400FC85C) for class and kind, and passes the descriptor to sub_1400EF9EC / sub_1400E5F78. I: its role in battle presentation follows the descriptor shape only; that it feeds the banner is not established (?).
open_questions: ? the producer of the descriptor the banner shows for an ability cast; ? how a scene task message reaches the banner, if it does.

name: BattleMsgEntry
summary: One slot of the battle message store: the kind, the kind-dependent argument, a message id and a 512-byte text buffer. The store is 40 entries at 0x20C stride after the message object's +8 (20,960 bytes); the dispatcher fills a slot and the resolver reads it back.

members.name: kind
members.text: Message kind (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9 and above were read). Kinds 4 and 9 resolve an item name; kind 6 an ability name.

members.name: arg
members.text: Kind-dependent argument: a number (kind 1), a unit record or battle unit index (2, 3), an item id (4, masked with 0x7FF; 9), an ability id (6), or an id + 0xB7C4 (7).

members.name: message_id
members.text: The kind-6 resolver stores id + 10000 here, a table-172 message id; no other writer was read.

members.name: text
members.text: The resolved text buffer: the resolver copies a name or a message into it (cap 511) and returns this address.

behavior.text: an entry is 0x20C bytes from the message object's +8; a slot above 0x27 returns null, so the store is 40 entries (20,960 bytes).
the dispatcher writes the kind and the argument; the kind setters (kinds 1, 3, 6, 9) write +0 and +4; the resolver writes +0xC and, for kind 6, +8.
Battle_Init clears 0x51E0 bytes at the object's +8, the whole store.

the argument filler reads the same storage as one flat record (struct BattleMsgRecord), so its dword offsets run across entry boundaries; this per-entry view is the one the setters and the resolver use.

notes: V: the store sits at g_BattleMsgObject + 8. The text buffer is the entry's exact remainder (0x20C - 0xC = 0x200 = 512 bytes).
open_questions: ? the use of +8 outside kind 6; ? whether every kind uses +4 the same way.

name: BattleMsgRecord
summary: The record the message object holds at +8: the values the argument filler reads for a message. Only the fields the filler touches are known; the names and roles below are inferred from that use.

members.name: kind
members.text: Selector matched against 4 and 9 when the message needs an item name (argument filler).

members.name: actor_index
members.text: Index into g_BattleUnitTable (512-byte stride); the filler reads the unit's data through it. Its low 11 bits are the item id when kind is 4.

members.name: name
members.text: Actor or record name used as a string argument. Length and encoding not established.

members.name: field_214
members.text: Read for some message ids; meaning not established.

members.name: fields_218
members.text: A run of dwords read from here for some message ids; count and meaning not established.

members.name: field_41C
members.text: Read for some message ids; meaning not established.

members.name: field_4184
members.text: Read for some message ids; meaning not established.

behavior.text: the offsets are the dword indices the filler uses (0, 1, 3, 133, 134.., 263, 4193) times 4; the fields the filler does not read are not listed.

notes: V: Battle_Init clears 0x51E0 bytes at the message object's +8. I: that block is the record storage, so the record is at most 20960 bytes. ?: the record's exact size and the fields between the listed offsets.
open_questions: ? the meaning of +0x214, +0x218, +0x41C and +0x4184; ? the name string's length and encoding.

name: BattlePanelHandWord
summary: One hand word as the flag-aware panels read it: the item id in bits 0..8 and a two-bit value in bits 14..15. The carrier is a 64-byte copy of a party or battle record's +0x30..+0x6F, at 0x141876E90 (field) or 0x141D3B880 (battle), with the five words at +0x24; it is not a field at unit+0x1EC.

members.name: item_id
members.text: Item id of the slot, masked with 0x1FF by the panel loops (0x14032F160, 0x140399E0C). 0xFF means empty and a value of 0x105 or more ends the walk.

members.name: slot_flags
members.text: Two-bit value taken with shift 12 and mask 0xC (shr 0xC at 0x14032F178/0x140399E24, and 0xC at 0x14032F17D/0x140399E29) and stored in dword_14184B228 / dword_140D40978. On the session carriers only bit 15 is ever set; bit 14 exists on the shop/menu list entries.

members.name: unused
members.text: No reader uses them; I: padding between the 9-bit panel id and the two flags.

behavior.text: the panels walk five words at carrier +0x24 (0x141876EB4 / 0x141D3B8A4), not at unit+0x1EC. The carrier is a copy: JobScreen_RefreshAfterChange copies record +0x30..+0x6F to 0x141876E90 (0x1402BD15D), PartyUnit_ReloadEquipment copies the live words to +0x24 (0x1402BDB42), and sub_14033E394 copies a battle record to 0x141D3B880 (0x14033E412).
two panel variants extract the top two bits: sub_14032EDB8 (task 9 over g_EquipCandidates, task 10 over 0x141876E90) and sub_140399A64 (over 0x141D3B880).
the id field is nine bits here, narrower than the party hand word, so the panel caps the id at 511 even before the flags are considered.

notes: V: the byte census of the equip session flags. The earlier placement at unit+0x1EC was wrong: the bytes show a record copy at 0x141876E90 with the hands at +0x24.
open_questions: ? what the two-bit value selects in the text draw, and whether a stock session ever leaves bit 14 set in the copied hand word.

name: BattleRangeMarkRecord
summary: One record of g_BattleRangeMarks, parallel to BattleTileRecord (512 records, layer 1 at +0x500).

members.name: reach
members.text: Non-zero = inside the range being built (a spread value range + 1 - distance, or 1); BattleRange_FlagTargetTiles turns it into tile flag +5 bit 0x40.

members.name: frontier
members.text: Set on tiles BattleRange_SpreadDiamond spreads from on its next pass.

behavior.text: with the target prompt up, the tiles with byte 0 non-zero were the yellow ones (records_battle_prompts).

notes: Detail and evidence: the function sheets linked from this page.
open_questions: ? bytes 2..4.

name: BattleSnapshot
summary: The 668,112-byte battle image a kind-1 resume entry carries, as the capture builds it in g_BattleState: a battle context, five blocks (A..E), the 21 x 512-byte unit records and 3,000 more bytes of scene-task state. Only the unit records hold object ids in bulk; the blocks are copied byte for byte and most of the image is never written.

members.name: context
members.text: Battle entry context: a pointer plus seven scene variables and an argument dword.

members.name: sub_object_1
members.text: Set up by a constructor call during the capture; shape not decoded.

members.name: sub_object_2
members.text: A 1 KB sub-object built by the same constructor; 45 nonzero bytes in the observed capture.

members.name: block_a
members.text: A 10,240-byte event-script file image (the buffer at 0x140D3CD50); item and job ids appear only as operands inside the script bytecode.

members.name: block_b
members.text: 887 u16 values: a per-map word table built from 24-byte static map records and indexed by scene variable 39; identical in all 24 payloads checked.

members.name: unit_records
members.text: 21 x 512 bytes from g_BattleUnitTable: job at +3, skillsets at +18/+19, abilities at +20/+22/+24, seven item words at +26..+39, name key at +508.

members.name: block_c
members.text: 512 eight-byte tile records of the battle map, indexed x + y * width; flag and movement-cost bytes only.

members.name: extra_capture
members.text: 3,000 bytes copied from 0x14114A4F0: 12-byte-ish entries with fill words; no id field identified.

members.name: block_d
members.text: Nine 168-byte scene-task data slots at 0x14114B150; captured but never restored.

members.name: no_work_copy
members.text: No slot work copy ends the snapshot: from +0x994EC the bytes are zero in every observed battle entry (no slot header), and block E lies inside that range at +0xA0418. An earlier reading that the last 40,164 bytes repeat the work copy was wrong.

members.name: block_e
members.text: The battle action state at 0x1418716A0: the current action word at +2 (an ability id masked to 10 bits), unit and action flags, and the wide action tables.

behavior.text: the capture writes 32 intervals, not the whole image; the largest never-written span is 501,656 bytes, so those bytes keep what an earlier battle left there and are still copied back on load.
the restore reads 117 sites; block D has no restore site and is reloaded by the scene-task path instead of from the image.
the only item ids are the 147 equipment words of the 21 unit records; the action word stores an ability id and an item use derives the item as the action number minus 128.
the image holds absolute pointers (the context pointer and a heap pointer at the start of the body), so it is a same-build snapshot and not a portable format.
blocks A, B, D and E carry no object id of their own because their writers are scene, map and action code rather than item or job stores; block C is a tile table.

notes: An earlier reading placed block E at 0x9F418. The capture's destination for 0x1418716A0 lands at g_BattleState + 0xA0418 and ends exactly where the tail fields begin, so 0xA0418 is the block and the older offset is 4,100 bytes of stale data.
open_questions: ? the shape of the 20 x 512-byte block at 0x3D51 (zero in the observed capture); ? the role of the 3,000-byte capture; ? the id content of block B's high bits and of block E's inner tables.

name: BattleTileRecord
summary: One tile of the battle map in g_BattleTileTable: 256 records per layer, two layers (layer 1 at +0x800), index x + y * width. Only the bytes the reach and target code reads are listed.

members.name: surface
members.text: Low 6 bits 0x3F: BattleRange_FlagTargetTiles never flags the tile (I: no surface, e.g. an unused layer-1 record).

members.name: height
members.text: Counted twice in the half-step heights of the reach rules (I: the height in whole steps; the HUD 'Height' agrees).

members.name: slope_depth
members.text: Bits 0..4 add to the half-step height; bits 5..7 times 2 add to a target's height and only conditionally to the attacker's (Unit_GetReachHeight). I: bits 0..4 slope / half step, bits 5..7 water depth.

members.name: corners
members.text: Four 2-bit fields, one per edge (shift 0 = the +x edge, 2 = -x, 4 = -y, 6 = +y): the edge's height is 2 * height + slope * field in half-steps (the move-range builder). (corners & 5) equal to 1 or 4 marks a one-axis slope for Battle_MoveRange_InitTiles.

members.name: flags5
members.text: Bit 0x40 set by BattleRange_FlagTargetTiles on the targetable tiles (I: the yellow mark). Bit 0x20 = a lit Move tile, written by Battle_MoveRange_Commit (live, 2026-11-05 and the 2026-11-09 captures). Low 5 bits: the tile's thickness in height steps; its underside is 2 * (height - thickness) half-steps (Battle_MoveRange_CeilingAbove).

members.name: flags6
members.text: Bit 0x01: BattleRange_FlagTargetTiles skips the tile; bit 0x02: BattleRange_MarkWeaponReach clears its weapon mark. Meaning ?.

behavior.text: the reach code reads it through g_BattleTileTable + 8 * (x + y * width + 256 * layer), width and height from g_BattleMapSize.

notes: Detail and evidence: the function sheets linked from this page.
open_questions: ? bytes +1 and +7 (not read by the reach or move-range code).

name: ClutBank
summary: One of the 14 banks of the palette manager (g_ClutManager, from +8): 16 rows of 16 colours with a timer per row, the state of every colour and the bank's base rows.

members.name: header

members.text: A copy of the 20-byte action record of the ability (or zero for a chemist item), made by Mem_CopyChecked with size 0x14 (0x140309BAC, 0x140309D49); its byte +8, the record's own formula byte (block +0x2C), is never read from here (the resolver reads the record). name: GUINodeState
summary: One state (timeline) of a component: its clock, its loop range, its flags and the channel sets and entries it applies. Created by GUINode_NewState from a 208-byte pool slot, filled by GUIComponent_LoadDef / UIAnim_PlayStateTracks, started by GUINode_PlayState, advanced by GUINodeState_Advance and applied by GUIComponent_ApplyStateAnims. The states of a component are the vector at component +616 .. +624.

members.name: name_key
members.text: The state's name (UIName_Assign / UIName_SetKey); GUINode_FindState matches the interned id at +8.

members.name: transition_key
members.text: Set by GUIComponent_LoadDef from the state record; when its id at +0x18 is non-zero GUIComponent_ApplyStateAnims applies a previous state first, and passes this key to the component lookup.

members.name: prev_component
members.text: Component of the previous state (the own component when its id at +0x28 is 0).

members.name: prev_state
members.text: Name of the previous state (the state's own name when its id at +0x38 is 0).

members.name: transition_delay
members.text: Frames before the transition's state applies: the previous state is sampled at (time - delay) once time >= delay.

members.name: record_flags
members.text: Written from the state record's int at +4 by GUIComponent_LoadDef; -1 in a fresh object. What reads it is not known.

members.name: rate
members.text: Clock multiplier, 1.0 in a fresh object; GUINodeState_Advance adds dt * rate to time.

members.name: time
members.text: Clock in seconds. GUINodeState_Advance: time = (dt * rate) + time; a loop or jump sets it to target / 60.0.

members.name: frame
members.text: Current frame = time * 60.0, a float (not an integer count). GUIComponent_ApplyStateAnims samples every active state at this value; for a state driven by a link GUIAddon_OnStateEvent writes it.

members.name: prev_frame
members.text: The frame at the previous tick (the jump-marker and keyframe-event tests compare against it); equals frame when the state did not advance.

members.name: frame_count
members.text: Frames of the state (the record's +28), the loop end when the range is unset.

members.name: range_start
members.text: Loop range start; the range counts only when range_start < range_end, otherwise the range is 0 .. frame_count.

members.name: range_end
members.text: Loop range end.

members.name: enabled
members.text: 1 = the state takes part in GUINode_UpdateStates and GUIComponent_ApplyStateAnims. 1 in a fresh object; GUINode_StopState clears it.

members.name: running
members.text: Set by GUINode_PlayState; GUINodeState_Advance advances only while it is set and clears it at a non-looping end.

members.name: dirty
members.text: Set by GUINode_PlayState and by the link writer; cleared by GUINodeState_Advance. While set GUINodeState_IsPastEnd answers false.

members.name: paused
members.text: 1 = the clock does not advance (a parent link drives the frame). GUINode_PlayState on a paused state only clears it.

members.name: loop
members.text: 1 = at the end frame the state restarts at the range start. From the UIB record's byte +32 at load; UIAddonFingerCursor_PlayLoop sets it for the cursor's Loop.

members.name: keep_alive
members.text: GUINode_UpdateStates keeps advancing a state that is past its end while this is set; the rest of its meaning is open.

members.name: hold
members.text: 1 = the state does not advance and counts as past its end (GUINodeState_IsPastEnd); cleared by GUINode_PlayState.

members.name: absolute
members.text: 1 = sampled values replace the node's fields, 0 = they are combined with them. 1 for every state loaded from a UIB timeline.

members.name: created
members.text: Set to 1 by GUINode_NewState; its reader was not found.

members.name: owners
members.text: Owner ids that receive the state's events (GUIOwners_PostEvent). GUINode_NewState puts the component's own id here.

members.name: channels
members.text: One channel set per target node (begin +0x90, end +0x98): the key tracks GUINode_ApplyAnimChannels samples (track pointers a[6] .. a[31]).

members.name: entries
members.text: Begin +0xB0, end +0xB8: the jump markers, triggers, state links and resets of the state.

members.name: field_C8
members.text: Zero in a fresh object; no reader found.

summary: The ten saved item order lists: 16-bit words in static storage, no header and no length word. Five item-menu lists (A0..A4) sit in scattered arrays reached through one pointer table; five equip and obtain-order lists (B0..B3 and B4) form one contiguous block. The save carries A as five copies and B as one 1010-byte copy.

members.text: Item-menu order, group 0 (weapons and shields). Live at 0x1407B2550, 282 bytes; 139 stock ids can enter it, so two entries are spare.

members.name: item_user_sort3

members.name: item_user_sort4
members.text: Item-menu order, accessory. Live at 0x1407B2500, 68 bytes; 33 stock ids, one spare.

members.name: item_user_sort5
members.text: Item-menu order, thrown weapons. Live at 0x1407B26B8, 42 bytes; six stock ids, fifteen spare.

members.name: equip_user_sort_hand
members.text: Equip-screen order for the hand, with the same membership as the first item-menu list. Live at 0x141874540.

members.name: equip_user_sort_head
members.text: Equip-screen order for the head. Live at 0x14187465A.

members.name: equip_user_sort_armor
members.text: Equip-screen order for the body. Live at 0x141874696.

members.name: equip_user_sort_accessory
members.text: Equip-screen order for the accessory slot. Live at 0x1418746E2.

members.name: item_get_order_sort
members.text: Obtain order, the only list with the whole id range as its membership. Live at 0x141874726, 524 bytes; 258 stock ids, four spare.

behavior.text: the end of every list is a word equal to 0xFF (255) or at least 0x105 (261). Ids 0..254 and 256..260 are therefore storable and only 255 is not, although 0xFFFF is the terminator of the separate menu list.
no list stores a length. The initialiser writes the 0xFF terminator into all ten, zeroes the whole B block from a zeroed 1010-byte template and then rewrites six of the eight sort-field byte lists.

the five A lists are reached through the pointer table at 0x14067F498 (a second table at 0x140689C38 holds the same five pointers); the B lists through the table at 0x14067FA90, and the obtain-order list starts 0x1E6 bytes into the block.

the membership writers insert a newly owned id at index 0 and shift the tail right with no capacity check. A3 ends flush against the mode-1 sort bytes and A1 has only two spare words before A4, so one word too many changes a neighbour rather than a spare entry.

the save pack writes A0..A4 as five fixed-size copies at 0x8A6C, 0x8B86, 0x8BC2, 0x8C0E and 0x8C52, and the whole B block as one 1010-byte copy at 0x8C7C; the load and the repair pass read the same six.
a second syncer (sub_14039684C) maintains the same lists from the inventory snapshot instead of the live counts, and reaches the obtain-order writer by a tail jump.
the stock id counts (139, 29, 37, 33, 6 and 258) leave 2, 1, 1, 1, 15 and 4 spare, so a stock save cannot exercise the insert-without-capacity path.

members.name: index_buffer

name: SaveManager
summary: The two singletons the save path runs on, with the fields it uses: the save-I/O state object that holds the frame step's command and sub-state, and the save manager object that holds the 50-slot image the `fftsave.bin` payload is built from. The offsets below name the object each field belongs to.

members.name: command
members.text: The step the frame step will run: 1 store, 2 load, 3 image to cache (0 idle).

members.name: sub_state
members.text: Phase of the current step: its progress inside the case the frame step is running.

members.name: image
members.text: The 50-slot image, 2,008,200 bytes: the payload of `fftsave.bin` on a store and the source of the cache after a load (1528 decimal).

members.name: game_save_data
members.text: The GameSaveData sub-object the entry queue writes into (904 decimal).

behavior.text: the frame step reads the command from the save-I/O state object and runs one case; the UI callbacks only set the command, so the screen never touches the container.
the image is a mirror of the cache: a store copies the cache into it, a load copies it back (2,008,200 bytes), so the two always hold the same 50 slots.
the sub-state is a phase counter rather than a retry count, because a step that finishes clears the command instead of incrementing it.

notes: The save-I/O state object is qword_140D405B8 and the manager is qword_143CD9EE0; the request object qword_140C69698 is a third object (SaveRequestRecord).
open_questions: ? the other fields of the save-I/O state object, and whether +0x108 is ever nonzero at the start of a frame.

name: SaveRequestRecord
summary: One queued file request of the save container manager: the consumer object, the entry name, the delivery buffer and its status. The queue is a vector on qword_140C69698 (first +0x40, last +0x48) of 328-byte (0x148) records, guarded by the critical section at +0x10 of the same object.

members.name: size
members.text: Size of the delivered payload (the entry minus its 16-byte header).

members.name: data
members.text: The delivered payload; the delivery allocates it with the record's heap.

members.name: heap
members.text: Allocator the delivery copies the payload with.

members.name: obj
members.text: The object the entry is delivered to: its +624 buffer and +632 size receive the payload.

members.name: name
members.text: Entry name, NUL-terminated; this is what the read kick filters on.

members.name: flag
members.text: Handed to the delivery call unchanged (0 in the requests observed).

members.name: status
members.text: Delivery status; 0 on the normal path.

behavior.text: a read request is pushed by sub_140033CBC with the object and the name, and served by sub_140033DF0, which copies the entry's 16-byte header into the object, calls the object's handler, then runs the object's post-delivery step.
the records are contiguous at stride 328 between the vector's first and last pointers, so a service can walk first..last and compact the ones it served.
the same queue carries the manual slot request (`fftsave.bin`), the settings request and every autosave entry, so one read kick serves them all.
a request that no kick serves stays queued until a later load or until the object is destroyed.

notes: The queue object also holds the busy flag at +392 and a byte at +602 that is cleared before a request, so a request made while a container write is in flight returns an error string.

members.text: Status set: the statuses the unit is immune to = job row status_b | equipment status_b. Status_FilterPendingSets drops them from a pending add; Unit_ReinitStatusCountdowns removes the always-on ones from it.

members.name: status_effective
members.text: The effective status set the behaviour code tests: always innate_status_a | applied_status (Battle_StatusApply, Battle_StatusRefresh, Unit_ReinitStatusCountdowns, Unit_ReloadFromJobRow all end with that OR). Byte 2 is status_16_23 below. A job row's status_c is copied here only until the next recompute.

members.name: status_countdown
members.text: Remaining duration (CT ticks) of the statuses 24..39, byte = id - 24: started from the property table (+3) by Unit_SetStatusCountdown, decremented once per engine pass for battle-applied, non-innate statuses (Battle_TurnEngine phase 4); Doom (byte 15) counts at the unit's turn start.

members.name: charge_counter
members.text: The remaining charge time of a Readying or Jumping unit (0xFF = none); Battle_StatusResolve sets 0xFF when none of Readying, Jumping, Performing is set.

members.name: pending_status_add
members.text: The statuses the action or event in progress wants to give (result block +29): written by the formulas, the turn-start rules, the tile effects and event opcode 0x92; consumed by Battle_StatusResolve and cleared by Battle_ResultResetStatusSets.

members.name: pending_status_remove
members.text: The statuses the action or event in progress wants to take away (result block +34); Status_FilterPendingSets limits it to applied statuses that are not innate.

members.name: applied_status
members.text: The statuses applied in battle: the only set Battle_StatusApply sets and Battle_StatusRefresh clears (the engine decrements the countdown of its timed members).

members.name: passive_bits
members.text: Passive-ability bit map, 88 bits for the ids 422..509 (bit 0x80 >> (index & 7) of byte +0x94 + (index >> 3), index = id - 422); the last three bytes (+0x9C..+0x9E) are the ones also listed below as move_flags_c, move_flags_d and move_flags.

members.name: passive_bits_halve_mp
members.text: Byte 5 of the passive map: bit 0x80 (id 462) halves the MP cost of an action (sub_1402828E4, sub_14030B1A0); bit 0x40 (id 463) is the JP Boost test of the JP award.

members.name: move_flags_c
members.text: Bit 0x02: Battle_MoveRangeSetup sets the jump to 31 (no height limit).

members.name: move_flags_d
members.text: Battle_MoveRangeSetup: bits 0x0C select Teleport (cleared for Toad / Chicken); 0x10 keeps the unit out of water; 0x02 makes the weather-dependent terrains cost 1; 0x01 makes every enterable terrain cost 1.

members.name: move_flags
members.text: Bit 0x08 raises the reach height like Float; bits 0x80 / 0x40 add the tile's water depth / depth - 2 (Unit_GetReachHeight). Battle_MoveRangeSetup picks the movement mode from it: 0x04 Fly, 0x08 float, 0x20, 0x80, 0x40, 0x10 the lava and water modes (record MoveRangeScratch). I: movement-ability flags.

members.name: unlock_mask
members.text: Unlock bits (Unit_AwardJobJp rebuilds them after an award).

members.name: learned
members.text: Learned-ability bits.

members.name: job_levels
members.text: Job level nibbles.

members.name: jp
members.text: Current JP (Unit_AwardJobJp adds to it).

members.name: total_jp
members.text: Total JP.

members.name: confirm_result
members.text: The result of the target-confirm shape routine (sub_140206F90): -1 drops the confirm, 0 or 1 opens the target confirmation (battle state 25), 2 starts the charge motion, 3 and above do nothing.

members.name: action_request
members.text: The unit's pending 20-byte action block (+1 command byte, +2 ability id u16). Only four direct stores write it (BattleAction_BuildUnitRequest 0x1402832AD, sub_1402831D8 0x140283235, Formula_37_RendEquipment 0x140307EB9 and its restore 0x140307EED); every other copy (the request queue, BattleAction_BuildReaction, BattleAction_ReleaseCharged, Battle_ExecuteSecondaryAction, BTurn_PreviewAction, the AI current action) is a call of Mem_CopyChecked with size 0x14. BTurn_PreviewAction saves and restores it around a preview.

members.name: action_command
members.text: The command (skillset) byte of the request (index into g_CommandKind; 18 = jump); TurnList_InsertEntry writes bit 0x20 of a turn entry when it is 18. A byte holds sets up to 253. The name token of the command is 0xB000 plus this byte (BattleMsg_UnitTurnScene 0x14023750F).

members.name: action_ability
members.text: The ability word of the request; the turn order and the action message read it; BTurn_PreviewAction restores the block.

members.name: mount
members.text: Bit 7: Unit_GetReachHeight adds 2 and reads the flags of the record at slot (low 5 bits). I: riding, the low bits the mount. Battle_MoveRangeSetup also reads bit 6 with the low 5 bits (a unit paired with the acting unit is not an obstacle).

members.name: side
members.text: Battle_MoveRangeSetup compares bits 0x30 of every other unit's byte +0x05 with this byte of the acting unit: different = the other side (an obstacle). I: the side the unit currently fights for.

behavior.text: UnitWork_CopySaveFields fills the arrays from a save record; UnitWork_StoreToSaveSlot writes them back.
the Toad restriction on abilities tests status byte +0x63 mask 0x02 (sub_1402828E4, sub_14030B1A0): a Toad unit may use only ability 0, 367 and 29 (a command kind of 10 never).
the passive-ability map is rebuilt by Unit_BuildAbilityBits; see PassiveAbilitiesAreAPerUnitBitMap.
